title: Add traceable container shipment reference snapshots
description: Add one canonical repository record for explicit shipment references associated with the existing container booking, pre-loading and loading-list chain. First audit and reuse any equivalent persisted relationship already present rather than creating a competing shipment master. Capture only user-recorded operational evidence; do not contact carriers, infer links from text, assert customs status, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation audits the existing booking, pre-loading and loading-list entities and ends with one canonical shipment-reference model explicitly linked to authoritative records rather than matching container, order or document numbers heuristically.

Users can maintain bounded optional evidence for shipment mode, carrier booking or shipping-order reference, bill-of-lading reference, origin, transit and destination ports, planned departure and arrival timestamps, carrier, forwarder, trucking provider and customs-broker snapshots where available.
Shipment mode uses an explicit supported value such as LCL, FCL or unknown; missing values remain empty or unknown and are never defaulted from container type, volume, customer, route or free text.
Server validation enforces bounded plain text, supported values and coherent planned timestamps while preserving optional fields when authoritative evidence is unavailable.
Links to booking, pre-loading or loading-list records are validated server-side; deleted, incompatible or unrelated records are rejected and are not silently reassigned.

Recorded snapshots remain readable if a referenced master or dictionary entry later changes or becomes unavailable, and edits preserve an auditable prior-value or revision trail rather than silently rewriting historical evidence.
Creating or revising shipment references does not change Sales Orders, Purchase Orders, container workflow status, inventory, finance, invoice, tax, customs or settlement records.
Existing container records without shipment-reference evidence remain readable without request-time or production backfill.
Repository schema changes are idempotent, normal list and detail queries are bounded or paged and avoid per-row database access, and validation uses only permitted local or test-database paths.

Unit/integration tests cover each supported mode, partial evidence, explicit source linkage, invalid or deleted sources, timestamp and text validation, revision history, legacy records, bounded queries and adjacent-record non-mutation; safe validation passes and browser acceptance is recorded as deferred during development.

scenarios: Open an existing container chain, record FCL or LCL shipment references with a partial route and planned dates, and verify the evidence remains linked to the selected authoritative records without changing their workflow status.
Leave unavailable references empty, attempt an invalid source link or incoherent planned dates, verify rejection, then revise valid evidence and confirm the prior recorded values remain auditable.

human_gate.reason: Repository-only operational shipment-reference evidence and non-production test schema. Carrier, customs, production database, deployment and release actions remain behind mandatory human gates.
